body.statement: For every admissible fixed bounded model \(\Theta\), each fixed \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), and every nonempty shell \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)\), the estimator \(\widehat\beta\) has worst-case squared error at most a constant times \(\min\{B^2,(n\lambda_n^2)^{-1}\}\).  With \(t_{\alpha_0}\) chosen from the fixed model envelopes, the corrected interval \(\mathcal C_n\) has coverage at least \(1-\alpha_0\) uniformly on \(\mathcal D_\rho\) and worst-case expected length on the shell at most a constant times \(\min\{B,(\sqrt n\lambda_n)^{-1}\}\), without knowing \(r\).  Moreover, for every \(d\geq1\), \(E\geq d+2\), \(R_{\max}\geq d+2\), and \(\delta>0\), there is one fixed compatible choice of \(\Theta\), common to all \(r\), for which the matching minimax lower bounds hold for squared error and for intervals honest on \(\mathcal D_\rho\) (indeed, for intervals honest on the shell alone).  On that experiment the two minimax quantities are therefore of the stated orders, and uniform consistency along a shell sequence holds if and only if \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\to\infty\).
body.justification: The theorem quantifies how quickly the exact identifying flag may approach the nonidentified boundary before estimation and honest inference fail.
body.gap: Causal Dantzig and environmental GMM give regular inference, while Andrews and Guggenberger give generic singularity-robust testing for supplied moments; none derives this structural rate frontier with an estimated cumulant plane and a full-observation causal lower-bound family.  The conversion of the testing rate into honest-interval length is an incremental standard consequence rather than a separate novelty claim.
body.consumer: The rate converts an empirical flag magnitude in protein-signaling environments into a principled precision and consistency diagnostic.
body.proof_tex:
We prove the proposed claim in two parts.  The upper bounds are uniform over every fixed admissible bounded model.  The lower bounds are proved on one fixed compatible model, as the claim now says; mere nonemptiness under arbitrary numerical envelopes does not imply that a particular least-favorable family fits those envelopes.

\emph{Uniform cumulant estimation.}
Let \(s_0=2R_{\max}+\delta\).  The coefficient bounds imply
\[
 |\gamma|\leq a_1q_1.
\]
The structural equations, the source \(s_0\)-moment envelope, the triangle inequality in \(L^{s_0}\), and Lyapunov's inequality therefore give a constant \(K_0<\infty\), depending only on the fixed model bounds, such that
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\max_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \mathbb E_\theta\bigl(|T_e|^{s_0}+|Y_e|^{s_0}\bigr)\leq K_0. \tag{26}
\]
Here all divisions by \(\alpha\) are licensed by \(|\alpha|\geq a_0>0\).

For clarity, an unbiased joint-cumulant estimator can be written explicitly.  For variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\), each equal to \(T_e\) or \(Y_e\), the population identity obtained by differentiating the log moment generating function is
\[
 \operatorname{cum}(X_1,\ldots,X_k)
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_k}(|\pi|-1)!(-1)^{|\pi|-1}
   \prod_{D\in\pi}\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{j\in D}X_j\right]. \tag{27}
\]
For a partition \(\pi=\{D_1,\ldots,D_s\}\), replace its product of expectations by
\[
 \frac{1}{(n_e)_s}
 \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_s\ {
m distinct}}
 \prod_{a=1}^s\prod_{j\in D_a}X_{j,e,i_a}.           \tag{28}
\]
Independence of distinct observations shows directly that (28) is unbiased.  Symmetrizing (27)--(28) produces the stipulated cumulant U-statistics.  The square of every summand uses total degree at most \(2k\leq2R_{\max}<s_0\), so (26) and H\"older's inequality bound its second moment uniformly.  In the variance double sum, pairs of ordered index tuples with disjoint index sets have zero covariance; only \(O(n_e^{2s-1})\) of the \(O(n_e^{2s})\) pairs overlap.  Thus, for a uniform constant \(K_1\),
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta
 \left(\lVert\widehat c_k-c_k\rVert_2^2+
       \lVert\widehat m_k-m_k\rVert_2^2\right)
 \leq \frac{K_1}{n},
 \qquad 2\leq k\leq R_{\max},                       \tag{29}
\]
once \(n_e\geq R_{\max}\).  We used \(n_e\geq\underline\pi n\) and the fact that \(E,R_{\max}\) are fixed.  Formula (26) also bounds all population cumulants in (29), through (27).

Put \(H=\widehat C-C\).  On \(\lVert H\rVert_{\rm op}\leq\kappa_0/2\), every unit vector \(x=Cy\) in \(A\) has \(\lVert y\rVert\leq1/\kappa_0\), and hence lies within \(\lVert H\rVert_{\rm op}/\kappa_0\) of \(\operatorname{col}(\widehat C)\).  Conversely, the variational definition of the smallest singular value gives directly
\[
 \sigma_d(\widehat C)
 =\inf_{\lVert y\rVert=1}\lVert(C+H)y\rVert
 \geq\sigma_d(C)-\lVert H\rVert_{\rm op}
 \geq\kappa_0/2.
\]
The same approximation argument in the reverse direction therefore gives distance at most \(2\lVert H\rVert_{\rm op}/\kappa_0\).  Taking suprema over unit vectors in the two subspaces yields
\[
 \lVert\widehat Q-Q_A\rVert_{\rm op}
 \leq \frac{4}{\kappa_0}\lVert H\rVert_{\rm op}.    \tag{30}
\]
On the complementary event the left side is at most two, while Markov's inequality and (29) make that event's probability \(O(n^{-1})\).  Hence
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta
 \lVert\widehat Q-Q_A\rVert_{\rm op}^2\leq K_2/n.   \tag{31}
\]

For \(|b|\leq B\), define
\[
 g_k(b)=Q_A(m_k-bc_k),\qquad
 \widehat g_k(b)=\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-b\widehat c_k),
\]
and
\[
 \Delta_n=\max_{d+2\leq k\leq R_{\max}}
 \sup_{|b|\leq B}\lVert\widehat g_k(b)-g_k(b)\rVert_2.
\]
The exact decomposition
\[
 \widehat g_k(b)-g_k(b)
 =\widehat Q\{(\widehat m_k-m_k)-b(\widehat c_k-c_k)\}
  +(\widehat Q-Q_A)(m_k-bc_k)                         \tag{32}
\]
and (29)--(31), together with the population cumulant bounds following (29), imply
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathbb E_\theta\Delta_n^2\leq K_3/n. \tag{33}
\]
There are only finitely many values of \(k\), so taking the displayed maximum changes only the constant.

\emph{Estimation and honest inversion.}
The cumulant-cancellation lemma gives, for every \(\theta\in\mathcal D_\rho\),
\[
 g_k(b)=(\beta-b)Q_Ac_k,
 \qquad g_k(\beta)=0.                                \tag{34}
\]
The objective defining \(\widehat\beta\) is no larger at its minimizer than at \(\beta\).  If \(r^\star=r\), equations (32)--(34) consequently give
\[
 |\widehat\beta-\beta|\,\lVert Q_Ac_r\rVert_2
 =\lVert g_r(\widehat\beta)\rVert_2
 \leq2\Delta_n.                                     \tag{35}
\]
Since both effects lie in \([-B,B]\), (33), (35), and the shell lower bound yield
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \mathbb E_\theta(\widehat\beta-\beta)^2
 \leq K_4\min\left\{B^2,\frac{1}{n\lambda_n^2}\right\}. \tag{36}
\]
The finitely many sample sizes for which some \(n_e<R_{\max}\) are covered by increasing \(K_4\), because \(n_e\geq\underline\pi n\), the effect error is at most \(2B\), and shell strengths are uniformly bounded by (26)--(27).

Choose the deterministic calibration radius so that
\[
 t_{\alpha_0}^2\geq K_3/\alpha_0.                    \tag{37}
\]
Denote the displayed norm-sublevel set in the corrected interval definition by \(\mathcal R_n\).  This is a proof intermediate, not an additional model object.
On the event \(\Delta_n\leq t_{\alpha_0}/\sqrt n\), (34) places the true \(\beta\) in the raw inversion set \(\mathcal R_n\).  By (33), (37), and Markov's inequality, this event has probability at least \(1-\alpha_0\), uniformly over \(\mathcal D_\rho\).  The singleton fallback in the corrected definition is used only when \(\mathcal R_n\) is empty, which cannot happen on this event.  It therefore does not alter this coverage bound.  The small-sample full interval also covers.  This proves uniform honesty without inverting any influence covariance.

Each constraint defining \(\mathcal R_n\) is a sublevel set of the norm of an affine function of the scalar \(b\), hence is convex; their intersection with \([-B,B]\) is an interval.  If \(b,b'\in\mathcal R_n\), then (32)--(34) and the shell condition imply
\[
 |b-b'|\lambda_n
 \leq\lVert g_r(b)-g_r(b')\rVert_2
 \leq2\left(\frac{t_{\alpha_0}}{\sqrt n}+\Delta_n\right). \tag{38}
\]
When \(\mathcal R_n\) is empty, the corrected fallback is a singleton and has length zero.  Thus (33), (38), Cauchy--Schwarz, and the deterministic box bound give
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \mathbb E_\theta\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_n)
 \leq K_5\min\left\{B,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\lambda_n}\right\}. \tag{39}
\]
Both (35) and (38) use the true breakout order only in the analysis; the procedures maximize over all admitted orders and do not know \(r\).

\emph{A compatible full-observation lower-bound experiment.}
It remains to construct one fixed model on which (36) and (39) cannot be improved.  Choose coefficient and moment bounds with strict slack around the following compact family; this is possible because the family below is fixed and has uniformly finite source moments.  Put
\[
 J=[19/10,23/10],\quad a=3,
 \quad
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}2&5\\5&14\end{pmatrix},
\]
and, for \(b\in J\), set
\[
 f_b=\frac{5-2b}{3-b},\qquad
 g_b=\frac1{3-b},\qquad z_b=b-1.                     \tag{40}
\]
All denominators and all three variances are bounded away from zero on \(J\).  If \(V_b,W_b,Z_b\) are independent centered Gaussians with these variances, then direct calculation gives
\[
 f_b+g_b=2,\qquad 3f_b+bg_b=5,\qquad
 9f_b+b^2g_b+z_b=14.                                 \tag{41}
\]
Thus
\[
 G_b=(V_b+W_b,,3V_b+bW_b+Z_b)\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma) \tag{42}
\]
for every \(b\in J\).

Independently, let \(L_e\) be a centered bounded-jump compound-Poisson source whose jump-\(j\) rate is increased by \(\eta\) only in environment \(e=j\leq d\), with all other rates at a common positive baseline.  Define
\[
 U_e=L_e+V_b,quad \epsilon_{t,e}=W_b,quad
 \epsilon_y=Z_b,quad \alpha=1,quad\beta=b,quad\gamma=3-b. \tag{43}
\]
Before the perturbation below,
\[
 (T_e,Y_e)=(L_e,3L_e)+G_b,                            \tag{44}
\]
so its complete law is independent of \(b\).  The calibration matrix has leading block \(\eta V_d\), and its plane is \(A=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf e_1,\ldots,\mathbf e_d\}\).

For the prescribed \(r\), let \(\operatorname{He}_r\) be the probabilists' Hermite polynomial and put
\[
 h_r(x)=e^{-x^2}\operatorname{He}_r(\sqrt3x),\qquad
 \mu_r=\frac{r!}{3^{(r+1)/2}}.                       \tag{45}
\]
If \(N\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), the substitution \(u=\sqrt3x\) and the Rodrigues identity
\(\operatorname{He}_r(u)\phi(u)=(-1)^r\phi^{(r)}(u)\) give, by \(r\) integrations by parts,
\[
 \mathbb E[N^kh_r(N)]
 =3^{-(k+1)/2}\mathbb E[N^k\operatorname{He}_r(N)]
 =\begin{cases}0,&k<r,\\ \mu_r,&k=r.\end{cases}     \tag{46}
\]
The boundary terms vanish because a polynomial times a Gaussian density tends to zero.  Both \(h_r\) and \(h_r'\) are bounded.

Only in the spare environment \(e=d+1\), replace the density of \(W_b\) by
\[
 p_{b,\lambda}(w)=\phi_{g_b}(w)
 \left\{1+\frac{\lambda}{\mu_rg_b^{r/2}}
 h_r\!\left(\frac{w}{\sqrt{g_b}}\right)\right\}.    \tag{47}
\]
Because \(J\) and the set of orders are compact and finite, respectively, boundedness in (45) permits one \(\lambda_0>0\) for which the bracket in (47) lies in \([1/2,3/2]\) for all \(b\in J\), all admitted \(r\), and \(0<\lambda\leq\lambda_0\).  Equations (46)--(47) show separately that this is a probability density, is centered, preserves all moments below \(r\), and increases the \(r\)-th raw moment by exactly \(\lambda\).  Since all lower moments are fixed, the cumulant formula (27) shows that the \(r\)-th cumulant also increases by exactly \(\lambda\).  Gaussian domination makes the moment generating function entire and gives uniform moments of every fixed order.

The perturbation leaves \(C\) unchanged because \(r\geq d+2\), and it gives
\[
 Q_Ac_r=\lambda\mathbf e_{d+1},\qquad
 Q_Am_r=b\lambda\mathbf e_{d+1}.                     \tag{48}
\]
All lower projected contrasts vanish.  Choose once and for all a calibration gap below \(\eta\sigma_d(V_d)\), coefficient boxes containing (43), and a moment envelope strictly exceeding the compact supremum just established.  Then every law in (43)--(48), for every admitted \(r\) and \(0<\lambda\leq\lambda_0\), belongs to the same \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda)\).

We next bound the likelihood of the complete observed data.  Under the Gaussian law (42),
\[
 \mathbb E_b[W_b\mid G_b=x]=\ell_b^\top x,\qquad
 \ell_b^\top=g_b(1,b)\Sigma^{-1},                    \tag{49}
\]
and
\[
 \tau_b^2=\operatorname{Var}_b(W_b\mid G_b)
 =g_b-g_b^2(1,b)\Sigma^{-1}(1,b)^\top
 =-\frac{(b-1)(2b-5)}{3(b-3)^2}>0.                   \tag{50}
\]
The last inequality holds uniformly on \(J\).  The tilted density of \(G_b\) is
\[
 \phi_\Sigma(x)\{1+\lambda R_b(x)\},
 \quad
 R_b(x)=\frac{1}{\mu_rg_b^{r/2}}
 \mathbb E\!\left[
 h_r\!\left(\frac{\ell_b^\top x+\tau_bN}{\sqrt{g_b}}\right)
 \right].                                            \tag{51}
\]
The coefficient functions in (49)--(51) are continuously differentiable on \(J\), \(g_b\) and \(\tau_b\) are bounded away from zero, and \(h_r,h_r'\) are bounded.  Differentiating the right side of (51) under the standard-normal expectation is justified by the dominating random variable \(K(1+\lVert x\rVert+|N|)\), and gives
\[
 |R_b(x)|\leq K_6,\qquad
 |\partial_bR_b(x)|\leq K_7(1+\lVert x\rVert).       \tag{52}
\]
The constants are uniform over the finite set of \(r\).  The mean-value theorem and the finite Gaussian second moment now imply
\[
 \int\{R_b(x)-R_{b'}(x)\}^2\phi_\Sigma(x)\,dx
 \leq K_8|b-b'|^2.                                  \tag{53}
\]
After reducing \(\lambda_0\) so that \(\lambda_0K_6\leq1/2\), (51)--(53) yield
\[
 \chi^2(P_{b,\lambda}^{G},P_{b',\lambda}^{G})
 \leq2K_8\lambda^2|b-b'|^2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{b,\lambda}^{G},P_{b',\lambda}^{G})
 \leq\chi^2(P_{b,\lambda}^{G},P_{b',\lambda}^{G}).  \tag{54}
\]
The second inequality follows from \(\log x\leq x-1\).  Adding the independent \(L_e\) and applying the common map in (44) cannot increase relative entropy, chi-square divergence, or total variation.  For the first two claims, condition the likelihood ratio on the observed image and apply Jensen's inequality respectively to \(x\log x\) and \((x-1)^2\); for total variation, take suprema over inverse images.  Only observations in the spare environment change with \(b\).  Product likelihood ratios also give
\[
 1+\chi^2(P_{b,\lambda}^{,n},P_{b',\lambda}^{,n})
 \leq\exp\{K_9n\lambda^2|b-b'|^2\}.                 \tag{55}
\]

For densities \(p,q\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \lVert P-Q\rVert_{\rm TV}
 =\frac12\int|p/q-1|q
 \leq\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(P,Q)}.                    \tag{56}
\]
Choose \(b,b+h_n\in J\), where
\[
 h_n=c\min\left\{B,\frac1{\sqrt n\lambda}\right\}, \tag{57}
\]
and choose the fixed \(c>0\) small enough that (55)--(56) make the total variation at most a number
\[
 v<\min\{1/2,1-2\alpha_0\}.                          \tag{58}
\]
For any estimator, let \(D\) be the event that it is closer to \(b\) than to \(b+h_n\).  On \(D^c\) its squared error at \(b\) is at least \(h_n^2/4\), and on \(D\) its squared error at \(b+h_n\) is at least \(h_n^2/4\).  The definition of total variation gives
\[
 \max_{j=0,1}\mathbb E_j(\widehat\beta-\beta_j)^2
 \geq\frac{h_n^2}{8}(1-v).                          \tag{59}
\]
If an interval has coverage \(1-\alpha_0\) at both laws, then under the first law the two endpoint-inclusion events have intersection probability at least \(1-2\alpha_0-v\).  On that intersection its length is at least \(h_n\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_0\operatorname{length}(\mathcal I_n)
 \geq h_n(1-2\alpha_0-v).                            \tag{60}
\]
This proves both desired lower bounds for \(0<\lambda\leq\lambda_0\), using full observed-data laws in the same shell.

For completeness, stronger nonempty shells also contain an ordinary parametric lower-bound path.  The moment bound and (27) imply a fixed \(\Lambda<\infty\) with \(\lVert Q_Ac_r\rVert\leq\Lambda\).  Take any member of a nonempty shell, retain its \(\alpha\), latent and treatment source laws, and choose a fixed \(q\in(q_0,q_1)\), \(\gamma=\alpha q\), and an invariant independent Gaussian outcome noise of sufficiently small fixed variance.  Vary \(\beta\) over a nontrivial interval inside \([-B,B]\).  None of \(C,A,r^\star\), or the shell strength changes.  In the augmented experiment observing \((U,T,Y)\), a change \(h\) in \(\beta\) changes only the conditional Gaussian mean of \(Y\) by \(hT\), and direct integration of the Gaussian likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_\beta^n,P_{\beta+h}^n)
 \leq \frac{h^2}{2\sigma_y^2}\sum_e n_e\mathbb E[T_e^2]
 \leq K_{10}nh^2.                                   \tag{61}
\]
Marginalizing \(U\) can only decrease this quantity by the conditional Jensen argument used after (54).  To convert (61) to total variation without an external premise, map the two laws to the event attaining total variation.  Binary relative entropy as a function of its first probability has second derivative at least four; Taylor's theorem therefore gives \(\operatorname{KL}(P,Q)\geq2\lVert P-Q\rVert_{\rm TV}^2\).  Choosing \(h=c\min\{B,n^{-1/2}\}\) and repeating (59)--(60) gives lower bounds of orders \(\min\{B^2,n^{-1}\}\) and \(\min\{B,n^{-1/2}\}\).  Since \(\lambda_0\leq\lambda\leq\Lambda\), these are, up to fixed constants, the claimed \(\lambda\)-dependent orders.

Combining (36), (39), (59)--(61) proves the two minimax equivalences on the compatible fixed experiment.  If \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\to\infty\), (36) gives uniform mean-square consistency.  Conversely, if this divergence fails, a subsequence has \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\) bounded, and (57)--(59) give a strictly positive minimax risk on that subsequence.  No uniformly consistent estimator then exists.  This proves the final if-and-only-if assertion.
